atlas-ie.0120: The fund administrators and banks hiring in Dublin work in English; multilingual operations roles at multinationals add German, Dutch, French or Swedish.
atlas-ie.0121: The Big Four graduate pages read (KPMG, Deloitte, EY) state no language requirement beyond English, which is the language of the application and interviews; no certificate is asked.
atlas-ie.0122: Only 2.4 to 2.8% of Irish job postings say English is not required, so English is the working language; recruiters report the most requested second languages in sales and support roles are German, Dutch, Swedish and French.
atlas-ie.0123: Technology employers in Dublin and Cork work in English; the technical stack (Python, JavaScript, C/C++) is what is tested, not a language certificate.
atlas-ie.0124: Just over 80% of the class of 2024 were in work nine months after graduating (HEA); Eurostat puts the employment rate of 20-to-34-year-olds with a tertiary degree at 91.6% in 2025 and 92.0% for those who left education within three years.
atlas-ie.0125: The vacancy rate stayed low at 1.3% in the last quarter of 2025 (1.2% a year earlier), against 3.9% in the Netherlands and 3.5% in Belgium.
atlas-ie.0126: No source read gives a return-offer or conversion rate for Irish work placements or graduate programmes, nor a time to first job for internationals.
atlas-ie.0127: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens, and British citizens under the Common Travel Area, need no visa, work permit or immigration registration to live, study or work in Ireland.
atlas-ie.0128: Apply for a PPS number (tax and social security) on MyWelfare, then add your job in Revenue myAccount before the first payday.
atlas-ie.0129: Without that, the first salary is taxed at the emergency rate, about 52% with USC; it is refunded once Revenue issues your payroll notice.
atlas-ie.0131: The course must be on the official list of eligible programmes (ILEP). Visa-required nationals apply for a study visa; others, US citizens included, show their documents at the border and register within 90 days.
atlas-ie.0132: Since 13 January 2025 every first registration is in person at Burgh Quay in Dublin, for €300 a year.
atlas-ie.0133: Work 20 hours a week in term and 40 only from 1 June to 30 September and from 15 December to 15 January; no self-employment, delivery riding included.
atlas-ie.0134: Ireland did not adopt the EU student-mobility rules: a student permit from another EU country gives no right to study here.
atlas-ie.0135: Funds, courses of 8 months or more
atlas-ie.0140: Money paid into the account just before applying is treated as not genuine and leads to refusal.
atlas-ie.0141: An internship that is an accredited part of your Irish course, up to half its length, can be full time with no work permit.
atlas-ie.0142: Students of foreign universities in a critical-skills field need an Internship Employment Permit, for up to 12 months, paid at least the minimum wage, and must return to finish their degree.
atlas-ie.0145: Apply within six months of your final results, while your Stamp 2 is still valid: 12 months after an honours bachelor’s, 12 plus 12 after a master’s or PhD.
atlas-ie.0146: Full-time employed work with no work permit, but no self-employment; this time counts towards citizenship, unlike student years. Before it ends you need an employment permit from an employer.
atlas-ie.0150: A job on the critical skills list with a relevant degree, or any eligible job at the higher salary; a contract of at least two years and no labour-market test. At least half the employer’s staff must be from the EEA or UK.
atlas-ie.0151: Your spouse joins at once and may work; after 21 months you move to Stamp 4 and no longer need a permit. You may change employer after nine months.
atlas-ie.0153: €40,904 a year; €36,848 within 12 months of graduating
atlas-ie.0156: Permit fee (employer cannot pass it on)
atlas-ie.0157: A contract of 12 or 18 months is refused: it must be at least 24 months or permanent.
atlas-ie.0159: The employer first advertises for 28 days on JobsIreland/EURES and on one more site; the 50:50 staff rule applies. A spouse can join after 12 months and, since May 2024, works without a permit of their own.
atlas-ie.0160: €36,605 a year; €34,009 for Irish graduates of the last 12 months
atlas-ie.0162: €500 up to six months, €1,000 up to 24
atlas-ie.0164: The research institution signs the agreement; no work permit is needed, the visa is free, the spouse joins at once with the right to work, and Stamp 4 follows after 21 months.
atlas-ie.0165: A PhD on a stipend is a student on Stamp 2, and the stipend is free of income tax, USC and PRSI.
atlas-ie.0169: US citizens have an intern working-holiday scheme with Ireland, aged 18 to 30, for 12 months: temporary work only, at most six months with one employer, and no conversion to a work permit inside Ireland.
atlas-ie.0171: Only for citizens of Argentina, Australia, Canada, Chile, Hong Kong, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea and Taiwan aged 18 to 30 (35 for Canada, Australia and New Zealand), within yearly quotas: 12 months (24 for Canadians).
atlas-ie.0172: Ireland is outside Schengen: the border officer stamps up to 90 days. US and other visa-free nationals enter with a passport; others need an Irish short-stay visa, except Chinese and Indian citizens holding a British-Irish visa (BIVS). No work is allowed.
atlas-ie.0174: Nothing to arrange in advance: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens, and British citizens under the Common Travel Area, need no visa, work permit or immigration registration.
atlas-ie.0175: Ireland is outside Schengen: a residence permit from another EU country gives no right to enter or study here. Visa-required nationals apply online through AVATS (€60 single entry, €100 multiple); others travel with the full file and register on arrival.
atlas-ie.0176: Keep the file in your hand luggage for the border officer: passport, employment permit or admission letter with fees receipt, proof of housing and funds (€10,000 for students), and private health insurance.
atlas-ie.0177: Keep a valid proof of address for your PPS number and bank: a utility bill in your name, the Residential Tenancies Board registration letter, or an employer verification letter if you are newly hired.
atlas-ie.0178: None: there is no immigration registration for EU, EEA, Swiss or British citizens.
atlas-ie.0179: The border officer stamps permission for up to 90 days. Before it runs out, book an appointment at Burgh Quay in Dublin, now the one office for the whole country, for the Irish Residence Permit: €300, with fingerprints and photo, and the card arrives by registered post in 10 to 15 working days.
atlas-ie.0180: Apply for a PPS number on MyWelfare.ie with ID, a reason such as a work contract, and proof of address; an in-person identity check at an Intreo centre issues the Public Services Card, and the number arrives by post in 4 to 10 working days.
atlas-ie.0181: Then register on Revenue’s myAccount and add your job: otherwise you pay emergency tax of 40% plus 8% USC instead of the standard 20% with tax credits.
atlas-ie.0182: Your European Health Insurance Card covers you.
atlas-ie.0183: British citizens have the same access to public health care as Irish citizens under the Common Travel Area.
atlas-ie.0184: Students need private medical insurance covering at least €25,000 for accidents and €25,000 for illness, including hospital stays.
atlas-ie.0185: Renew the permit online before it expires (€300): the acknowledgement extends your previous rights, including work and health care, for up to 12 weeks.
atlas-ie.0186: Do not leave Ireland before you hold the plastic card: neither the appointment confirmation nor the renewal receipt is a travel document, and airlines refuse boarding on the way back.
atlas-ie.0187: Do not leave Ireland before collecting the IRP card: the appointment or renewal receipt is not a travel document, and airlines refuse boarding on the way back.
atlas-ie.0188: Renew online before your permission expires: the acknowledgement keeps your rights, work included, for up to 12 weeks.
atlas-ie.0189: Filing the general permit on day 27 of the advert means automatic refusal: wait the full 28 days.
atlas-ie.0190: Airlines and ferries ask for a passport even on direct UK–Ireland routes, although immigration law does not.
atlas-ie.0191: First registrations are only in Dublin and appointments are scarce, so some people pass the 90 days stamped at the border before getting one.
atlas-ie.0192: Social-welfare offices differ on accepting an employer’s letter as proof of address for the PPS number.
atlas-ie.0193: Many employers hire graduates on Stamp 1G but will not sponsor a permit at €40,904 when junior salaries are lower.
atlas-ie.0194: How fast start-ups backed by Enterprise Ireland or IDA get the two-year exemption from the 50:50 rule is not set.
atlas-ie.0195: The seasonal employment permit created in 2024 still waits for its regulations.
